---
title: "check-one-div-per-subfile.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags a Quarto subfile
holding more than one top-level div.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-18) is that new and revised content
gets one div per subfile, a solution in its own `_sol` file included.
This implements
[gha#1092](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1092).

A subfile is a `.qmd` file whose name starts with `_`
and which sits under a `_subfiles` directory.
The check reports a subfile that has more than one top-level fenced div
when the pull request adds a line to it.
The finding sits on the opening line of the second div.

The check does not count:

- a div nested inside another div;
- a top-level div whose id starts with `rem-source-`,
  a source remark that belongs right after the item it credits;
- anything inside a code fence
  (a backtick opener whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence;
  any indentation is accepted, for fences inside list items);
- anything inside an HTML comment;
- a div inside a blockquote,
  since a line starting with `>` neither opens a fence nor a div;
- the divs an `include` shortcode may pull in at render time,
  since the shortcode is not expanded.

It accepts any `_*.qmd` file under a `_subfiles` directory
and does not check the name form
(the older `_def-name.qmd` or the newer `_name_def.qmd`).

A touched subfile with a div, code fence or HTML comment that is never closed
is reported too, as an error when `fail` is true,
because the divs after it would go uncounted without notice.
A stray closing `:::` hides nothing and is ignored.
A file that matches `globs` but is not a subfile is not examined.
The run prints a notice with how many such files it skipped,
which includes any non-underscore `.qmd` file under `_subfiles`
because the default glob matches those.

## Scope

Only a subfile with a line a pull request adds is reported.
A touched subfile counts as revised,
so the whole file is parsed (a div opens far above the changed line)
and a one-line fix to a file that still holds an exercise and its solution
is reported.
An untouched subfile keeps its layout.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new, and a blank added line is not content.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked subfile in full on purpose,
which measures how many existing subfiles hold several divs.
Every run prints how many lines, subfiles and divs it examined.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default               | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*_subfiles/*.qmd'`  | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`                  | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`               | Fail the workflow when a subfile holds more than one top-level div. The default gives warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`               | Scan every tracked subfile in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`              | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | `'ubuntu-latest'` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-one-div-per-subfile.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a subfile (_subfiles/_*.qmd) that holds more than one
# top-level div when a PR adds a line to it. New and revised content gets one div
# per subfile, a solution in its own _sol file included. Warn-only by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check one div per subfile

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-one-div-per-subfile.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*_subfiles/*.qmd'              # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                             # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every subfile, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-one-div-per-subfile.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-one-div-per-subfile.yml)
for the full caller stub.
